verdict.reasoning: Patient reports cough and runny nose for ‘quite a few days’ and clarifies onset as ‘maybe five or six days ago’ along with ‘my nose is running.’
Patient describes cough as ‘so continuous… quite dry… all day… keeps me up at night’ and notes ‘the coughing is giving me a sore throat.’

Associated symptoms mentioned include runny nose (‘my nose is running’), chills (‘I’ve been having, like, shivers’), muscle pain (‘my muscle was really hurting… in my arms, my legs, like, just everywhere’), and lethargy/weakness (‘basically getting quite lethargic and weak’).
Patient denies breathlessness (‘I don’t feel breathless, no’), nausea and vomiting (‘No nausea, no vomiting’), and chest pain (‘Any pain in your chest?’ – ‘No, not that either.’).
Patient reports diarrhea at onset that resolved: ‘at the beginning… I had a little bit of diarrhea… Has that got better now…? – Yeah, yeah, it got better… then it stopped.’
She states ‘How’s your appetite?’ – ‘I mean, it’s okay… it didn’t cut my appetite or anything,’ indicating a currently normal appetite.
When asked about medical history, patient says ‘Well, I have type 2 diabetes.’
Patient also states ‘I have quite high blood pressure.’
Regarding medications: ‘I take Metformin for the diabetes.’
She continues, ‘And I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure.’
When asked about allergies: ‘Any allergies at all to medication?’ – ‘No allergies, no.’
Family history: ‘My dad also has type 2 diabetes.’
Social history: ‘In terms of your social situation, who lives at home with you?’ – ‘It’s just me and my partner.’ and ‘He has none of this… He’s fine,’ indicating an asymptomatic partner.
Employment: ‘What is it that you do for work?’ – ‘I am a developer.’; clinician replies ‘So you work in the IT field.’
Alcohol: patient drinks wine ‘maybe two or three glasses’ on ‘say, three evenings a week.’
Smoking: ‘Do you smoke at all, April?’ – ‘I used to, but I’ve stopped for about six months now.’

Clinician’s assessment: ‘I think, based on your story, I think essentially I think you’re going through a bit of a viral illness… you’ve had a bit of a cough, bit of a runny nose…’ – consistent with viral upper respiratory infection.

The noted findings (dry cough, runny nose, chills, muscle aches) are all described in the history and are typical for a viral URI, matching the rationale implied by ‘bit of a viral illness… cough… runny nose… feeling quite weak and lethargic.’
Clinician explicitly attributes the illness to a viral cause: ‘I think… you’re going through a bit of a viral illness. I don’t think there’s anything to worry about.’
Plan includes symptomatic care: ‘things you can do… get some nice rest, drink plenty of fluids, keep yourself well hydrated. You can take regular paracetamol.’

Follow-up instructions: ‘If you feel like it’s still any better in two to three days, it’s probably worth coming back to see me again… if you are still feeling feverish and your cough isn’t getting any better, then we may look to give you some antibiotics for your chest.’ This is monitoring with 2–3 day follow-up and possible antibiotics if no improvement/worsening.

Work/absence advice: ‘maybe take a day or two off work if you can get some good bed rest, and maybe think about work early next week’ and notes a ‘theoretical risk that you’re maybe slightly infectious still,’ indicating consideration of work absence for infectivity and rest.

Alcohol counseling: clinician notes her intake is near the recommended limit and advises reduction: ‘maybe something that you can maybe cut down on if you can… maybe for the first few weeks… cut down to two glasses a week and then one week thereafter…’ and links it to ‘because of your blood pressure and diabetes.’
